learn.hook: Your grandmother's chatai mat is a maths pattern! Strips go over and under in a rule.
points: To weave a paper mat, push a strip over one strip and under the next, again and again.
We can describe each row with a rule like 'over 1, under 1' or 'over 2, under 1'.
Often the next row starts one place later, so the pattern shifts. After some rows, the first row's pattern comes back.
With 'over 1, under 1', row 3 looks like row 1, so the pattern repeats every 2 rows.
To complete a pattern on grid paper, find the rule for each row and the shift from row to row.

example.q: Row rule: over 2, under 1. Each new row starts one square later. After how many rows does row 1 come back?
steps: The core is 3 squares long (2 over + 1 under)
Shifting by 1 each row, we go through 3 positions
So row 4 matches row 1: it repeats every 3 rows

learn.reallife: Baskets, chatai mats, khadi cloth and charpai ropes are all woven with over-under rules.

games.title: Continue the weave (O = over, U = under)

items.text: O O U O O U O O ___
Row 1: O U O U. Row 2 shifted by one: ___ O U O
O O U U O O U U O ___

games.title: Weaving facts
items: In 'over 1, under 1', the pattern repeats every 2 rows if each row shifts by one.
Row 3 is the same as row 1.
A weaving rule tells how many strips to go over and under.
Every weaving row must be the same as the row above.
Over 2, under 2 with a shift of 1 repeats every 4 rows.
The core is 4 long, so 4 shifts bring it back.

quiz.q: A strip goes over 1, under 1. If it starts with over, what does it do at the 6th crossing?
quiz.explain: Odd crossings are over and even crossings are under. 6 is even, so under.
steps: The rule is over 1, under 1, starting with over.
So odd crossings (1st, 3rd, 5th …) are over and even crossings are under.
6 is even, so the 6th crossing is under.
quiz.mistake: Counts from 0 instead of 1

quiz.q: Row rule: over 2, under 1. What is the 7th crossing if the row starts with over?
quiz.explain: The core O O U has 3 crossings. 7 = 3 + 3 + 1, so the 7th is like the 1st: over.
steps: The core is O O U: 3 crossings.
7 = 3 + 3 + 1, so after two full cores the 7th is the 1st of a new core.
The 1st of the core is over, so the 7th is over.
quiz.mistake: Does not count in cores

quiz.q: What is the rule for this row? O O U O O U O O U
quiz.explain: Two overs then one under repeat.
steps: Find the part that repeats: O O U, then O O U again.
That is two overs and one under.
So the rule is over 2, under 1.
quiz.mistake: Reads the pattern backwards

quiz.q: With 'over 1, under 1' and a shift of one each row, which row looks exactly like row 1?
quiz.explain: Row 2 is shifted, row 3 is shifted back, matching row 1.
steps: Row 1: O U O U … Row 2 shifts one place: U O U O …
Row 3 shifts one more place: O U O U … again.
So row 3 looks exactly like row 1.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the shifted row 2 is the same

quiz.q: With 'over 2, under 1' and a shift of one each row, after how many rows does the pattern repeat?
quiz.explain: The core is 3 long, so after 3 shifts it lines up again: row 4 = row 1.
steps: The core over 2, under 1 is 2 + 1 = 3 crossings long.
Shifting by 1 each row, the pattern goes through 3 positions.
Row 4 matches row 1, so it repeats every 3 rows.
quiz.mistake: Uses the number of overs

quiz.q: Row 1 is O U U O U U. Row 2 starts one place later. What does row 2 start with?
quiz.explain: Shifting one place, row 2 starts with what row 1 has at the end: U, giving U O U U O U.
steps: Row 1 is O U U O U U.
Shifted one place later, row 2 begins with row 1's last crossing: U O U U O U.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a shifted row starts the same

quiz.q: A pattern on grid paper has rows: ■□■□, □■□■, ■□■□, ___. What comes in row 4?
quiz.explain: Rows take turns: rows 1 and 3 are the same, so row 4 is like row 2.
steps: Row 1 ■□■□ and row 3 ■□■□ are the same; row 2 is □■□■.
quiz.mistake: Copies row 3 again

quiz.q: Which tool helps you check a weaving pattern before you weave?
options: Counting the colours of the strips
Drawing it row by row on grid paper
quiz.explain: Grid paper lets you draw each row with its rule and shift.
steps: A weaving pattern has a rule for each row and a shift.
Grid paper lets you draw each row square by square.
So draw it row by row on grid paper.
Answer: Drawing it row by row on grid paper
quiz.mistake: Does not see how to plan a pattern

teach.ask: Gappu wants to weave a mat with the rule 'over 1, under 1'. How do I make the second row?
teach.praise: I shift each row by one, and row 3 looks like row 1. A checked mat!
teach.nudge: Should row 2 start the same as row 1?

revise.summary: A woven mat follows a row rule like 'over 1, under 1', and each new row usually starts one place later. After as many rows as the core is long, row 1's pattern comes back.
focus: Describe a row with an over–under rule
Find a crossing far along a row
Find after how many rows the pattern repeats
remember: 'Over 1, under 1' repeats every 2 rows: row 3 = row 1
'Over 2, under 1' core is 3 long: row 4 = row 1
Use grid paper to plan each row
traps: Don't count from 0; the first crossing is crossing 1.
A shifted row does not start the same as row 1.

learn.hook: Look at a rangoli border or a saree edge. The same little design comes again and again. That is a pattern!
points: A repeating pattern has a part that repeats. We call it the core.
Find the core by looking for where the pattern starts again.
Shapes can repeat by kind, colour, size or by turning.
To find a far-away shape, count in cores. In ▲ ● ■ ▲ ● ■ the core has 3 shapes.

example.q: In the pattern ▲ ● ■ ▲ ● ■ …, what is the 10th shape?
steps: The 10th shape is the 1st shape of the next core

learn.reallife: Borders on sarees, bangles, tiles on a floor and beads on a necklace all show repeating patterns.

items.text: A B B A B B A ___

games.title: True or false?
items: A pattern can be made by turning the same shape again and again.
In red, blue, red, blue, …, the 9th colour is blue.
Odd places are red, so the 9th is red.
Nothing repeats. It grows by 2 each time.

quiz.q: What comes next? ▲ ● ▲ ● ▲ ?
quiz.explain: The core is ▲ ●. After ▲ comes ●.
quiz.mistake: Repeats the last shape instead of following the core

quiz.q: What is the core of this pattern? 🔴 🔵 🔵 🔴 🔵 🔵 🔴 🔵 🔵
quiz.explain: 🔴 🔵 🔵 is the part that repeats.
steps: Look for where the pattern starts again.
quiz.mistake: Picks only part of the core

quiz.q: In ■ ▲ ● ■ ▲ ● …, what is the 12th shape?
quiz.explain: The core has 3 shapes. 12 ÷ 3 = 4 full cores, so the 12th shape is the last in the core: ●.
quiz.mistake: Counts the shapes one by one and slips

quiz.q: The pattern ⭐ 🌙 🌙 repeats. How many stars are in the first 15 shapes?
quiz.explain: 15 shapes make 15 ÷ 3 = 5 cores. Each core has 1 star, so 5 stars.
quiz.mistake: Counts the moons, or counts all the shapes

quiz.q: Riya's rangoli border goes red, yellow, green, red, yellow, green, … What colour is the 20th tile?
quiz.explain: The core has 3 colours. 20 = 3 × 6 + 2, so the 20th is the 2nd colour: yellow.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to use the remainder to find the place in the core

quiz.q: Each arrow is the one before turned a quarter turn clockwise: ↑ → ↓ ? What comes next?
quiz.explain: A quarter turn clockwise from ↓ (down) points ← (left).
steps: Each arrow turns a quarter turn clockwise: up, then right, then down.
A quarter turn clockwise from down points left: ←.
quiz.mistake: Turns anticlockwise or turns a half turn

quiz.q: Kabir strings beads: 2 red, 1 white, 2 red, 1 white, … He uses 18 beads. How many are red?
quiz.explain: Each core has 3 beads, 2 of them red. 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cores. 6 × 2 = 12 red.
quiz.mistake: Thinks half the beads are red

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a repeating pattern?
options: A B A B A B
quiz.explain: 3 5 8 2 9 1 has no part that repeats.
steps: A repeating pattern has a core that repeats.
A B, 1 2 and ▲ ■ each repeat again and again.
3 5 8 2 9 1 has no part that repeats, so it is NOT a repeating pattern.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any list of things is a pattern

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What makes a pattern a repeating pattern?'
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! The core repeats again and again. Like my song!
teach.nudge: What happens again and again in a pattern? What do we call that part?

revise.summary: A repeating pattern has a core that repeats. Find the core where the pattern starts again, and count in cores to find a far-away shape.
focus: Find the core of a pattern
Find what comes next
Find the shape at a far position using cores
Count one kind of shape in many cores
remember: In ▲ ● ■ ▲ ● ■ the core has 3 shapes
The 10th shape: 3 cores make 9, so it is the 1st of the core
Shapes can repeat by kind, colour, size or turning
traps: Don't pick only part of the core.
Don't forget the remainder when finding a far position.

learn.hook: Make squares with matchsticks in a row. 1 square needs 4 sticks. Does 2 squares need 8? Try it!
points: In a growing pattern, each step changes by a rule.
Find the rule by checking how much it grows each time: 4, 7, 10 grows by 3.
Use the rule to find later steps without drawing everything.
Some patterns grow by adding more each time: 1, 3, 6, 10 adds 2, then 3, then 4.

example.q: Matchstick squares in a row: 1 square uses 4 sticks, 2 squares use 7, 3 squares use 10. How many sticks for 5 squares?
steps: The rule: add 3 sticks for each new square

learn.reallife: Stacks of laddoos, steps of a staircase and seats in a stadium often grow in patterns.

quiz.q: What comes next? 3, 6, 9, 12, ?
quiz.explain: The rule is add 3. 12 + 3 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of finding the rule

quiz.q: Matchstick squares in a row use 4, 7, 10, … sticks. How many sticks for 6 squares?
quiz.explain: Start with 4 and add 3 for each extra square: 4 + 3 × 5 = 19.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every square needs 4 new sticks (6 × 4 = 24)

quiz.q: Dots make triangles: 1, 3, 6, 10, … What comes next?
quiz.explain: It adds 2, then 3, then 4, so next add 5: 10 + 5 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds the same amount every time

quiz.q: Arjun builds towers of 2, 4, 8, 16 blocks. Each tower doubles. How many blocks in the next tower?
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 or adds 8 instead of doubling

quiz.q: Square dot patterns have 1, 4, 9, 16 dots. How many dots in the next square?
quiz.explain: The squares are 1×1, 2×2, 3×3, 4×4. Next is 5×5 = 25.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 each time

quiz.q: Matchstick triangles in a row: 1 triangle uses 3 sticks, 2 use 5, 3 use 7. How many sticks for 10 triangles?
quiz.explain: Each new triangle adds 2 sticks. 3 + 2 × 9 = 21.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each triangle needs 3 new sticks (10 × 3 = 30)

quiz.q: What is the rule? 5, 9, 13, 17, …
quiz.explain: Each number is 4 more than the one before.
steps: It grows by the same amount, 4, each time.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the first number

quiz.q: Meena counts down: 100, 90, 80, 70, … What is the 8th number?
quiz.explain: Each step takes away 10. The 8th number is 7 steps after 100: 100 − 70 = 30.
quiz.mistake: Takes 8 steps instead of 7

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How can I find the 20th step of a growing pattern without drawing it all?'
teach.praise: Chirpy cheer! Find the rule and use it again and again. No drawing needed!
teach.nudge: What stays the same from one step to the next? How do I use that?

revise.summary: In a growing pattern each step changes by a rule. Find the rule by checking how much it grows, and use it to find later steps without drawing.
focus: Find the rule of a growing pattern
Continue number and matchstick patterns
Find a far step using the rule
remember: 4, 7, 10 grows by 3
Matchstick squares: 4 + 3 × (squares − 1) sticks
1, 3, 6, 10 adds 2, then 3, then 4
traps: Don't think each new square needs 4 new sticks.
Don't add the same amount when the pattern adds more each time.

learn.hook: How do tiles cover a whole floor with no gaps? Some shapes are tiling champions!
points: Tiling means covering a flat surface with shapes with no gaps and no overlaps.
Squares, rectangles, equilateral triangles and regular hexagons can tile a floor on their own.
Circles always leave gaps. Regular pentagons also leave gaps.
Where corners meet at a point, they fill a full turn of 360°: 4 squares (4 × 90°), 3 hexagons (3 × 120°) or 6 triangles (6 × 60°).

example.q: A floor is 4 m long and 3 m wide. How many square tiles of side 1 m will cover it?

learn.reallife: Floor tiles, brick walls, honeycombs and chessboards are all tilings.

games.title: Can it tile on its own?
True or false?
items: Squares can cover a floor with no gaps.
Square tiles fit edge to edge, 4 at each corner.
Circles can tile a floor with no gaps.
Round edges always leave gaps between circles.
Bricks in a wall make a tiling of rectangles.
The bricks fit with no gaps and no overlaps.
Tiles in a tiling may overlap.
4 square corners fit exactly around one point.

quiz.q: Which shape cannot tile a floor on its own without gaps?
quiz.explain: Circles have curved edges, so gaps are always left between them.
steps: A tiling needs no gaps and no overlaps.
Squares, rectangles and equilateral triangles fit together with straight edges.
Circles have curved edges and always leave gaps: circle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any shape can tile if you push it close

quiz.q: In a floor of square tiles, how many squares meet at one corner point?
quiz.explain: Each square corner is 90°. 360° ÷ 90° = 4.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the full turn of 360°

quiz.q: Honeybees build their honeycomb with cells of which shape?
quiz.explain: Honeycomb cells are hexagons. They fit together with no gaps.
steps: Honeycomb cells fit together with no gaps.
quiz.mistake: Guesses circle because the cells look round from far

quiz.q: How many regular hexagons meet at one point in a hexagon tiling?
quiz.explain: Each hexagon corner is 120°. 360° ÷ 120° = 3.
steps: Corners at a point must make a full turn: 360°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the answer is 6 because a hexagon has 6 sides

quiz.q: A floor is 5 tiles long and 4 tiles wide. How many tiles cover it?
quiz.explain: 4 rows of 5 tiles: 5 × 4 = 20.
steps: The floor is 4 rows of 5 tiles.
quiz.mistake: Adds length and width instead of multiplying

quiz.q: In tiling, what does 'no overlaps' mean?
options: Tiles do not sit on top of each other
quiz.explain: Overlap means one tile covers part of another. A tiling has none.
steps: Overlap means one tile covers part of another.
So tiles do not sit on top of each other.
Answer: Tiles do not sit on top of each other
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 'overlap' with 'gap'

quiz.q: How many equilateral triangles meet at one point in a triangle tiling?
quiz.explain: Each corner of an equilateral triangle is 60°. 360° ÷ 60° = 6.
steps: Corners at a point must make 360°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the answer is 3 because a triangle has 3 corners

quiz.q: Aisha's bathroom wall needs 6 rows of 8 tiles. She has 40 tiles. How many more does she need?
quiz.explain: She needs 6 × 8 = 48 tiles. 48 − 40 = 8 more.
quiz.mistake: Gives the total needed instead of how many more

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is tiling? Why don't people use round tiles?'
teach.praise: Wow! Tiles must cover with no gaps and no overlaps. Round ones leave gaps!
teach.nudge: What must a tiling never have? What goes wrong with circles?

revise.summary: Tiling covers a flat surface with shapes with no gaps and no overlaps. Corners meeting at a point make a full turn of 360°.
focus: Know which shapes tile on their own
Find how many shapes meet at a point
Count tiles for a floor
remember: 4 squares (4 × 90°), 3 hexagons (3 × 120°), 6 triangles (6 × 60°) meet at a point
Circles and regular pentagons leave gaps
Tiles for a floor = tiles in a row × rows
traps: Don't use the number of sides: 3 hexagons meet, not 6.
Don't add length and width to count tiles; multiply.

topics.title: Which shapes fit around a point?

learn.hook: Five square tiles around one corner? Try it — something goes wrong! Let us see why.
points: Around a point, the angles of the tiles must add to a full turn (360°).
Five squares need 5 × 90° = 450°, which is more than a full turn, so they overlap.
A regular octagon has 135° corners. Two make 270°, leaving a 90° gap, so octagons cannot tile on their own. A square fills that gap!
Mixed tiling: 2 squares + 3 equilateral triangles fit around a point (180° + 180° = 360°).
To continue a mixed tiling, list the shapes around one corner and repeat the same order at every corner.

example.q: Can 2 regular hexagons and 2 equilateral triangles meet at a point?
example.answer: Yes, they fill a full turn

learn.reallife: Floors in old forts and temples have octagon-and-square tiles. Look out for them!

games.title: Fits around a point with no gap?

quiz.q: Why can't 5 squares meet at one point on a flat floor?
options: Their corners add to 450°, more than a full turn
They add to less than a full turn
quiz.explain: 5 × 90° = 450°, which is more than 360°, so they overlap.
steps: Corners around a point must add to exactly 360°.
450° is more than a full turn, so they overlap.
Answer: Their corners add to 450°, more than a full turn
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the corners must make exactly a full turn

quiz.q: What angle is left when 2 regular octagons (135° each) meet at a point?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 180° instead of 360°

quiz.q: Which shape fills the gap between 2 regular octagons at a point?
quiz.explain: The gap is 90°, exactly one square corner.
steps: A 90° gap is exactly one square corner: a square.
quiz.mistake: Does not work out the gap

quiz.q: How many equilateral triangles fit with 2 squares around a point?
quiz.explain: 2 squares take 180°. 360° − 180° = 180°. Each triangle is 60°, so 3 triangles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every gap takes 2 shapes

quiz.q: A tiling has 1 hexagon and some triangles at each corner. How many triangles?
quiz.mistake: Uses 6 triangles as in a triangle-only tiling

quiz.q: Do regular octagons tile a floor on their own?
quiz.explain: 2 octagons leave a 90° gap and 3 would need 405°. So they cannot tile alone.
steps: So No, octagons alone leave square gaps.
Answer: No, they leave square gaps
quiz.mistake: Thinks every regular shape tiles

quiz.q: At each corner of a tiling you see: square, triangle, square, triangle, triangle. Is it a full turn?
quiz.explain: Two squares (180°) and three triangles (180°) make 360°.
steps: That is a full turn, so yes.
quiz.mistake: Adds the angles wrongly

quiz.q: Rina cuts out squares and equilateral triangles of the same side. Which set around a point works?
quiz.explain: 2 × 90° + 3 × 60° = 360°. 3 squares + 2 triangles = 390°, too much.
steps: Square = 90°, triangle = 60°. The total must be 360°.
quiz.mistake: Does not add the angles

teach.ask: Gappu wants to tile his nest floor with octagons only. Will it work? What could help?
teach.praise: Octagons leave 90° gaps, so I will add little squares!
teach.nudge: What happens when two octagons meet at a corner?

revise.summary: Angles around a point must add to exactly 360°. Octagons leave a 90° gap that a square fills, and 2 squares with 3 triangles also fill a point.
focus: Check whether shapes fit around a point
Find the gap left by some shapes
Choose a set of shapes for a mixed tiling
remember: Square 90°, equilateral triangle 60°, hexagon 120°, octagon 135°
2 octagons + 1 square = 135 + 135 + 90 = 360°
2 squares + 3 triangles = 180° + 180° = 360°
traps: Don't subtract from 180°; a full turn is 360°.
5 squares make 450°, so they overlap.

learn.hook: Two identical triangles can join to make a square, a kite or a bigger triangle. Which triangles are they?
points: Joining two matching triangles along a side can make new shapes: a square, a rectangle, a kite, a parallelogram or a bigger triangle.
Equilateral triangle: all 3 sides equal and all 3 angles equal.
Isosceles triangle: 2 sides equal.
Scalene triangle: no two sides equal.
Right-angled triangle: one angle is a right angle (a square corner).

example.q: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm. What kind of triangle is it?
steps: Two sides are equal (5 cm and 5 cm)

learn.reallife: Samosas, roof trusses and road signs are triangles. Bridges use triangles because they are strong.

games.title: Triangle facts
items: An equilateral triangle has all angles equal.
All sides and all angles are equal.
A scalene triangle has two equal sides.
No two sides are equal in a scalene triangle.
A right-angled triangle has a square corner.
One angle is a right angle.
Two matching right-angled triangles can make a rectangle.
Join them along the longest side.
Many triangles have sides of different lengths.

quiz.q: A triangle has sides 6 cm, 6 cm and 6 cm. What kind of triangle is it?
quiz.explain: All three sides are equal, so it is equilateral.
quiz.mistake: Does not check all three sides

quiz.q: A triangle has sides 4 cm, 7 cm and 9 cm. What kind is it?
quiz.explain: No two sides are equal, so it is scalene.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any triangle with different numbers is isosceles

quiz.q: Which triangle has exactly two equal sides?
quiz.explain: 5, 5 and 8 has exactly two equal sides: isosceles.
steps: 5, 5, 5 has three equal sides; 3, 4, 5 and 5, 6, 8 have none.
quiz.mistake: Picks the equilateral one

quiz.q: A set square has one square corner. What kind of triangle is it?
quiz.explain: A triangle with a right angle is a right-angled triangle.
steps: A set square has one square corner.
A square corner is a right angle.
So it is a right-angled triangle.
quiz.mistake: Names it by sides only

quiz.q: An equilateral triangle has one angle of 60°. What are the other two angles?
quiz.explain: In an equilateral triangle all angles are equal.
steps: In an equilateral triangle all three angles are equal.
One angle is 60°, so the others are the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only the sides are equal

quiz.q: Two matching right-angled triangles are joined along their longest sides. Which shape can they make?
quiz.explain: The two right angles end up at opposite corners and the shape has 4 square corners: a rectangle.
steps: Join the two matching right-angled triangles along their longest sides.
The two right angles sit at opposite corners and the other corners fill square corners.
A shape with 4 square corners: a rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two triangles always make a bigger triangle

quiz.q: Two matching equilateral triangles are joined along a side. How many sides does the new shape have?
quiz.explain: Each triangle has 3 sides. The joined side is hidden: 3 + 3 − 2 = 4 sides.
quiz.mistake: Adds all the sides

quiz.q: Can a triangle be both right-angled and isosceles?
options: Only if all sides are equal
Only if it has two right angles
Yes, with two equal sides around the square corner
quiz.explain: Half of a square cut along its diagonal has a right angle and two equal sides.
steps: Cut a square along its diagonal.
Each half has a square corner and two equal sides around it.
So yes, with two equal sides around the square corner.
Answer: Yes, with two equal sides around the square corner
quiz.mistake: Thinks a triangle can have only one name

teach.ask: Gappu found a triangle with sides 3 cm, 3 cm and 4 cm. What is its name and why?
teach.praise: It is isosceles because two sides are equal!
teach.nudge: How many of its sides are equal?

revise.summary: Triangles are named by sides: equilateral (3 equal), isosceles (2 equal), scalene (none equal). A right-angled triangle has one square corner; one triangle can have two names.
focus: Name a triangle from its sides
Know equilateral angles are equal
See what shapes two matching triangles make
remember: Equilateral: all 3 sides and angles equal
Isosceles: 2 sides equal; scalene: no sides equal
Right-angled: one right angle
traps: Check all three sides before naming.
A triangle can be both right-angled and isosceles.

learn.hook: Is a square a rectangle? Is a rectangle a parallelogram? Let us sort out the four-sided family!
points: A kite has two pairs of equal sides that are next to each other.
A parallelogram has opposite sides equal and parallel (they never meet).
A rectangle is a parallelogram with all four angles right angles.
A square is a rectangle with all four sides equal.
So every square is a rectangle, and every rectangle is a parallelogram, but not the other way round.

example.q: A quadrilateral has sides 5 cm, 5 cm, 8 cm and 8 cm, with the two 5 cm sides next to each other. What is it?
steps: Each pair is next to each other

learn.reallife: Flying kites, chocolate bars, doors and chessboard squares are all members of the four-sided family.

games.title: Name the shape
pairs: Two pairs of equal sides next to each other

games.title: Family rules
items: A square has 4 right angles and opposite sides equal.
A rectangle can have unequal sides.
Its opposite sides are equal and parallel.
A kite has opposite sides equal.
Its equal sides are next to each other.
A parallelogram must have right angles.

quiz.q: A shape has opposite sides equal and parallel, but no right angles. What is it?
quiz.explain: Opposite sides equal and parallel is a parallelogram. Without right angles it is not a rectangle.
steps: Opposite sides equal and parallel → parallelogram family.
No right angles, so not a rectangle or square.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every parallelogram has right angles

quiz.q: Which shape has two pairs of equal sides next to each other?
quiz.explain: That is the rule for a kite.
steps: Two pairs of equal sides next to each other is the rule for a kite.
In a parallelogram or rectangle the equal sides are opposite.
quiz.mistake: Confuses 'next to each other' with 'opposite'

quiz.q: Which is true?
quiz.explain: A square has all a rectangle needs: 4 right angles and opposite sides equal.
steps: A rectangle needs 4 right angles and opposite sides equal.
A square has all of that (and equal sides too).
So every square is a rectangle (not the other way round).
Answer: Every square is a rectangle
quiz.mistake: Reverses the family order

quiz.q: A rectangle has all sides equal. What is its special name?
quiz.explain: A rectangle with all sides equal is a square.
steps: If all its sides are equal too, it is a square.
So its special name is square.
quiz.mistake: Does not link rectangles and squares

quiz.q: Sides are 6 cm, 4 cm, 6 cm, 4 cm going round, with 4 right angles. What is it?
quiz.explain: Opposite sides equal with all right angles: rectangle. Not all sides are equal, so not a square.
steps: Going round 6, 4, 6, 4: opposite sides are equal.
It has 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle.
Not all sides are equal, so not a square: rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Calls it a square

quiz.q: Sides going round are 3 cm, 3 cm, 7 cm, 7 cm. What is it?
quiz.explain: The equal sides are next to each other in pairs: a kite.
steps: Going round 3, 3, 7, 7: the equal sides are next to each other.
Two pairs of equal neighbouring sides is a kite.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any two pairs of equal sides make a parallelogram

quiz.q: Which shape is always a parallelogram?
quiz.explain: A rectangle has opposite sides equal and parallel.
steps: A parallelogram has opposite sides equal and parallel.
A rectangle always has opposite sides equal and parallel.
So the rectangle is always a parallelogram.
quiz.mistake: Thinks kites are parallelograms

quiz.q: How is a square different from other rectangles?
quiz.explain: All rectangles have right angles and opposite sides equal; only a square has all sides equal.
steps: All rectangles have 4 sides, right angles and equal opposite sides.
Only a square has all four sides equal.
So a square differs because all its sides are equal.
Answer: All its sides are equal
quiz.mistake: Names something all rectangles share

teach.ask: Gappu thinks a square cannot be a rectangle. Can you explain why it is one?
teach.praise: A square has 4 right angles and equal opposite sides, so it is a special rectangle!
teach.nudge: What does a shape need to be a rectangle?

revise.summary: A kite has two pairs of equal neighbouring sides. A parallelogram has opposite sides equal and parallel; a rectangle adds right angles; a square adds equal sides.
focus: Name quadrilaterals from sides and angles
Know which shape family includes which
Tell a kite from a parallelogram
remember: Every square is a rectangle; every rectangle is a parallelogram
Kite: equal sides next to each other
Parallelogram: opposite sides equal and parallel
traps: Not every rectangle is a square.
A kite is not a parallelogram.
Don't confuse 'next to each other' with 'opposite'.

learn.hook: Cut a rhombus into pieces and rebuild them. Can you make a triangle, a 4-sided shape and a 5-sided shape?
points: Measure all four sides with a ruler to classify a quadrilateral.
If opposite sides are equal, it is a parallelogram (or rectangle or square). If neighbouring pairs are equal, it is a kite.
On grid paper, draw a parallelogram by sliding the top side across: e.g. bottom from (0,0) to (4,0), top from (1,2) to (5,2).
Draw a kite by marking a line of symmetry and placing equal sides on both sides of it.
Cutting a rhombus along a diagonal gives 2 triangles. Cutting off one corner leaves a 5-sided shape.

example.q: A shape measures 6 cm, 3 cm, 6 cm, 3 cm going round with no right angles. What is it?
steps: No right angles, so not a rectangle

learn.reallife: Carpenters measure the sides and corners of doors and windows to make sure they are true rectangles.

games.title: Cut the rhombus
items: Cutting a rhombus along a diagonal gives 2 triangles.
The diagonal splits it into two.
Cutting off one corner of a 4-sided shape leaves a 5-sided shape.
The cut makes one new side and two new corners in place of one.
Two pieces of a rhombus can never make a new 4-sided shape.
The two triangles can be rejoined differently, for example into a parallelogram.
A rhombus has all four sides equal.
It is a parallelogram with equal sides.

quiz.q: A quadrilateral measures 7 cm, 4 cm, 7 cm, 4 cm going round. Which family does it belong to?
quiz.explain: Opposite sides are equal, so it is in the parallelogram family.
steps: Going round 7, 4, 7, 4: opposite sides are equal.
So it belongs to the parallelogram family.
quiz.mistake: Reads 'two pairs equal' as a kite without checking positions

quiz.q: A quadrilateral measures 5 cm, 5 cm, 9 cm, 9 cm going round. What is it?
quiz.explain: Equal sides are next to each other, so it is a kite.
steps: Going round 5, 5, 9, 9: equal sides are next to each other.
quiz.mistake: Ignores where the equal sides are

quiz.q: On grid paper a shape has corners at (0,0), (4,0), (5,2) and (1,2). What is it?
quiz.explain: The top side is the bottom side slid across: both 4 long and parallel. That makes a parallelogram.
steps: Bottom side (0,0)–(4,0) is 4 long; top side (1,2)–(5,2) is also 4 long.
The top is the bottom slid across, so they are parallel and equal.
So the shape is a parallelogram.
quiz.mistake: Thinks slanted sides make a kite

quiz.q: How do you draw a kite on grid paper?
options: Draw 4 equal sides with right angles
Draw two parallel lines of the same length
Draw a line of symmetry and put matching sides on both sides of it
quiz.explain: A kite is symmetric about one diagonal, so the sides on each side match.
steps: A kite is symmetric about one diagonal.
So draw that line of symmetry first.
Then put matching sides on both sides of it.
Answer: Draw a line of symmetry and put matching sides on both sides of it
quiz.mistake: Draws a square instead

quiz.q: A rhombus is cut along one diagonal. What pieces do you get?
quiz.explain: A diagonal joins two opposite corners and splits the shape into 2 triangles.
steps: A diagonal joins two opposite corners.
It splits the four-sided shape into two parts with 3 sides each.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the pieces are four-sided

quiz.q: One corner is cut off a rhombus with a straight cut. How many sides does the bigger piece have?
quiz.explain: One corner is replaced by a new short side with two corners, so 4 + 1 = 5 sides.
steps: Cutting off a corner removes that corner but adds one new short side.
quiz.mistake: Thinks cutting removes a side

quiz.q: Sides 6, 6, 6, 6 cm with no right angles. What is it?
quiz.explain: All sides equal without right angles is a rhombus.
steps: All four sides are equal (6 cm).
No right angles, so it is not a square.
All sides equal without right angles: rhombus.
quiz.mistake: Calls every equal-sided shape a square

quiz.q: The two triangles from a rhombus cut along a diagonal are rejoined so the cut sides do not touch. Which shape can they make?
quiz.explain: Matching triangles joined along another pair of equal sides make a parallelogram.
steps: The two triangles are matching (same size and shape).
Joining them along another pair of equal sides gives opposite sides equal and parallel.
quiz.mistake: Thinks pieces can only go back into the rhombus

teach.ask: Gappu measured a shape: 4 cm, 6 cm, 4 cm, 6 cm, with square corners. What is it, and how do I know?
teach.praise: Opposite sides equal and square corners — a rectangle!
teach.nudge: What do the side lengths and the corners tell me?

revise.summary: Measure all four sides to classify a quadrilateral: opposite sides equal is the parallelogram family, neighbouring pairs equal is a kite. Draw shapes on grid paper and see what cutting makes.
focus: Classify a quadrilateral from its side lengths
Draw a parallelogram and a kite on grid paper
Know the pieces made by cutting a rhombus
remember: Cutting a rhombus along a diagonal gives 2 triangles
Cutting off one corner of a 4-sided shape leaves 5 sides
All sides equal and no right angles: rhombus
traps: Check where the equal sides are, not just that there are two pairs.
Cutting off a corner adds a side; it does not remove one.

topics.title: Tangram and Which shape am I?

learn.hook: Seven little pieces can make a cat, a boat or a dancer! This ancient puzzle is called a tangram.
points: A tangram has 7 pieces: 2 large triangles, 1 medium triangle, 2 small triangles, 1 square and 1 parallelogram.
All the tangram triangles have one right angle and two equal sides.
Two small triangles can make the square, the medium triangle or the parallelogram.
In 'Which shape am I?', one clue may fit many shapes. Use all the clues together.
Example: 'I have 4 equal sides' fits a square and a rhombus. Adding 'I have 4 right angles' gives only the square.

example.q: Clues: I have 4 sides. My opposite sides are equal. I have no right angles. My sides are not all equal. Which shape am I?
steps: No right angles: not a rectangle or square
Not all sides equal: not a rhombus

learn.reallife: Children all over the world play with tangrams. Try making a house or a fish at home!

games.title: Which shapes fit the clue 'I have 4 equal sides'?

quiz.q: How many pieces are there in a tangram?
quiz.explain: 2 large + 1 medium + 2 small triangles + 1 square + 1 parallelogram = 7.
steps: Count the pieces: 2 large + 1 medium + 2 small triangles.
quiz.mistake: Forgets some pieces

quiz.q: How many triangles are in a tangram set?
quiz.explain: 2 large + 1 medium + 2 small = 5 triangles.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the large ones

quiz.q: Which tangram piece has 4 right angles?
quiz.explain: Only the square has four square corners.
steps: The triangles each have only one right angle.
The parallelogram has no right angles.
Only the square has 4 right angles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the parallelogram has right angles

quiz.q: Which two pieces together can make the tangram square?
quiz.explain: Two small triangles join along their long sides to make the square.
steps: The square can be split along its diagonal into 2 equal triangles.
Those match the two small triangles.
So 2 small triangles make the square.
quiz.mistake: Uses pieces of different sizes

quiz.q: How are all the tangram triangles alike?
options: Each has a right angle and two equal sides
They are all the same size
quiz.explain: They are all right-angled isosceles triangles, in different sizes.
steps: Every tangram triangle has a square corner.
The two sides around that corner are equal.
So each has a right angle and two equal sides.
Answer: Each has a right angle and two equal sides
quiz.mistake: Thinks they are all equilateral

quiz.q: Clue: 'I have 4 equal sides.' Which shapes fit?
quiz.explain: Both a square and a rhombus have 4 equal sides.
steps: A square and a rhombus both do.
So the clue fits the square and the rhombus.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a clue always fits only one shape

quiz.q: Clues: 'I have 3 sides. All my sides are equal.' Which shape am I?
options: Isosceles triangle with a short side
quiz.explain: 3 equal sides means an equilateral triangle.
steps: So I am an equilateral triangle.
quiz.mistake: Ignores one of the clues

quiz.q: Clues: '4 sides. Opposite sides are equal. 4 right angles. Sides not all equal.' Which shape am I?
quiz.explain: Opposite sides equal and right angles: rectangle. Sides not all equal: not a square.
steps: 4 sides, opposite sides equal: parallelogram family.
Sides not all equal: not a square. So rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Stops before using the last clue

teach.ask: Gappu read the clue 'I have 4 right angles'. He shouted 'Square!' Is he sure? What else could it be?
teach.praise: It could be a rectangle too! I need a clue about the sides.
teach.nudge: Which other shape has 4 right angles?

revise.summary: A tangram has 7 pieces: 5 right-angled isosceles triangles, a square and a parallelogram. In 'Which shape am I?', one clue may fit many shapes, so use all the clues together.
focus: Know the 7 tangram pieces
Make one tangram piece from others
Solve shape riddles using all clues
remember: 2 large, 1 medium, 2 small triangles, 1 square, 1 parallelogram
Two small triangles make the square, the medium triangle or the parallelogram
'4 equal sides' fits a square and a rhombus
traps: Don't stop before using the last clue.
Tangram triangles are not equilateral.

learn.hook: Fold a square paper twice and you have a kite! Draw two lines across a circle and you have a rectangle!
points: Fold a square along a diagonal, then fold two neighbouring edges onto that diagonal: the shape is a kite.
The fold line (diagonal) of a kite cuts it into 2 matching triangles.
A diameter goes across a circle through its centre. Joining the ends of two diameters makes a quadrilateral.
That quadrilateral is always a rectangle. If the diameters cross at right angles, it is a square.
To work out a circle design, look for the centre, the diameters and how far apart the points on the circle are.

example.q: Two diameters of a circle cross at right angles. You join their four ends. What shape do you get?
steps: Both diagonals are diameters, so they are equal
Equal diagonals crossing at right angles in the middle: square

learn.reallife: Rangoli and alpana designs often start with a circle and lines through its centre.

games.title: Circle and kite facts
items: Joining the ends of two diameters makes a rectangle.
The diagonals are equal and cut each other in half.
If the diameters cross at right angles, the shape is a square.
It is a rectangle with all sides equal.
A kite's fold line splits it into 2 matching triangles.
The kite is symmetric about it.
Joining the ends of two diameters can make a kite with unequal pairs.
A diameter passes through the centre.
That is what makes it a diameter.

items.text: A line through the centre from edge to edge is a ___
Ends of 2 diameters joined make a ___
Diameters at right angles give a ___
A kite folded on its line of symmetry shows 2 matching ___

quiz.q: Which shape do you get when you join the four ends of two diameters of a circle?
quiz.explain: The two diameters are equal and cut each other in half, which makes a rectangle.
steps: Two diameters are equal in length and cut each other in half at the centre.
A quadrilateral whose diagonals are equal and bisect each other is a rectangle.
So joining the ends gives a rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks crossed lines always make a kite

quiz.q: When does joining the ends of two diameters give a square?
options: When the diameters cross at right angles
quiz.explain: Diameters crossing at right angles make all four sides equal: a square.
steps: Joining the ends always gives a rectangle.
If the diameters also cross at right angles, all four sides become equal.
So it is a square when the diameters cross at right angles.
Answer: When the diameters cross at right angles
quiz.mistake: Thinks the size of the circle matters

quiz.q: How many matching triangles does the fold line split a paper kite into?
quiz.explain: The kite's line of symmetry splits it into 2 matching triangles.
steps: The fold line of a kite is its line of symmetry.
It cuts the kite into two halves that match.
quiz.mistake: Counts all the folds

quiz.q: A paper kite is made by folding a square. What kind of shape is a kite?
options: A quadrilateral with two pairs of equal neighbouring sides
quiz.explain: A kite has 4 sides with neighbouring sides equal in pairs.
steps: A kite has 4 sides, so it is a quadrilateral.
Its neighbouring sides are equal in pairs.
So a quadrilateral with two pairs of equal neighbouring sides.
Answer: A quadrilateral with two pairs of equal neighbouring sides
quiz.mistake: Forgets how many sides a kite has

quiz.q: A rangoli design has 8 equally spaced points on a circle joined to the centre. How many equal angles are made at the centre?
quiz.explain: 8 lines from the centre make 8 equal parts of the full turn.
steps: 8 lines go from the centre to the 8 points.
They split the full turn into 8 equal parts.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the points

quiz.q: Each of those 8 equal angles at the centre is how many degrees?
steps: The full turn at the centre is 360°.
It is split into 8 equal angles.
quiz.mistake: Divides 180° instead of 360°

quiz.q: To draw a square inside a circle with all four corners on the circle, what do you draw first?
quiz.explain: Their four ends are the corners of the square.
steps: The corners of the square must lie on the circle.
Ends of two diameters at right angles make a square.
So first draw two diameters at right angles.
Answer: Two diameters at right angles
quiz.mistake: Starts with lines that do not cross the centre

quiz.q: Points A and C are ends of one diameter; B and D are ends of another. What is true about AC and BD?
quiz.explain: All diameters of one circle are the same length.
steps: AC and BD are both diameters of the same circle.
Every diameter goes through the centre and equals 2 radii.
So they are equal in length.
Answer: They are equal in length
quiz.mistake: Thinks diameters can be different

teach.ask: Gappu drew two diameters in a circle and joined the ends. He got a rectangle. How could I get a square instead?
teach.praise: If my diameters cross at right angles, I get a square!
teach.nudge: How should the two diameters cross?

revise.summary: Folding a square makes a paper kite whose fold line splits it into 2 matching triangles. Joining the ends of two diameters of a circle always gives a rectangle, and a square if they cross at right angles.
focus: Know the shape made by two diameters
Draw a square in a circle
Find angles at the centre of a circle design
remember: All diameters of a circle are equal
Two diameters at right angles → square
8 equal angles at the centre: 360° ÷ 8 = 45°
traps: Don't divide 180° for angles at the centre; use 360°.
Crossed diameters make a rectangle, not a kite.

learn.hook: Paint a big cube made of 27 small cubes. How many small cubes get paint on 3 faces? 2 faces? None?
points: A net is a flat shape that folds into a solid. A cube's net has 6 squares.
In a row of 4 squares in a net, the 1st and 3rd fold to be opposite, and so do the 2nd and 4th.
A 3×3×3 cube has 27 small cubes. Keeping only the edges (a frame) leaves 8 corners + 12 edge cubes = 20, so 7 are removed.
Painted 3×3×3 cube: corners (8) have 3 painted faces, edge middles (12) have 2, face centres (6) have 1, and the very centre (1) has none.

example.q: A 4×4×4 cube frame keeps only its edges. How many small cubes are in the frame and how many were removed?
steps: Each of 12 edges has 2 middle cubes: 24

learn.reallife: A dice is a cube whose opposite faces add to 7. Its net shows which numbers end up opposite.

quiz.q: How many squares does a net of a cube have?
quiz.explain: A cube has 6 faces, so its net has 6 squares.
steps: A net has one square for each face.
So a cube net has 6 squares.
quiz.mistake: Counts edges or corners

quiz.q: A cube net has squares in a row: 1, 2, 3, 4, with 5 above square 2 and 6 below square 2. Which face is opposite 1?
quiz.explain: In a row of four, the 1st and 3rd squares end up opposite each other.
steps: In a row of four squares, the 1st and 3rd fold to be opposite.
quiz.mistake: Picks a square that touches 1

quiz.q: In the same net (row 1, 2, 3, 4; 5 above 2; 6 below 2), which face is opposite 5?
quiz.explain: 5 and 6 both join square 2, one above and one below, so they fold to opposite faces.
steps: 5 is above square 2 and 6 is below square 2.
When folded, one goes to the top and one to the bottom.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the squares above and below are neighbours

quiz.q: A 3×3×3 cube frame keeps only the cubes along the edges. How many small cubes are removed?
quiz.explain: Frame = 8 corners + 12 edge cubes = 20. 27 − 20 = 7 removed.
quiz.mistake: Gives the frame count instead

quiz.q: How many small cubes are removed to make a 5×5×5 cube frame?
quiz.mistake: Forgets that each edge has 3 middle cubes

quiz.q: A 3×3×3 cube is painted on all sides. How many small cubes have exactly 2 painted faces?
quiz.explain: The middle cube of each of the 12 edges has 2 painted faces.
steps: Cubes with exactly 2 painted faces sit in the middle of each edge.
A 3×3×3 cube has 1 middle cube on each of its 12 edges.
quiz.mistake: Counts the corners

quiz.q: In that painted 3×3×3 cube, how many small cubes have no paint at all?
quiz.explain: Only the very centre cube is hidden from every side.
steps: 27 small cubes: 8 corners, 12 edge middles, 6 face centres are all painted.
Only the centre cube has no paint: 1.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every cube touches the outside

quiz.q: In that painted cube, how many small cubes have exactly 1 painted face?
quiz.explain: The centre cube of each of the 6 faces has 1 painted face.
steps: Cubes with exactly 1 painted face are face centres.
Each of the 6 faces has 1 centre cube.
quiz.mistake: Counts all 9 cubes on one face

teach.ask: Gappu painted a 3×3×3 cube red. Which small cubes have 3 red faces, and how many are there?
teach.praise: The 8 corner cubes have 3 red faces each!
teach.nudge: Where on the big cube do three faces meet?

revise.summary: A cube's net has 6 squares; in a row of 4, the 1st and 3rd and the 2nd and 4th are opposite. In a painted 3×3×3 cube: 8 corners have 3 faces, 12 edge cubes 2, 6 face centres 1, and 1 centre has none.
focus: Find opposite faces in a cube net
Count cubes in a cube frame
Count painted faces of small cubes
remember: 3×3×3 frame: 20 cubes kept, 7 removed
Squares above and below the same square are opposite
traps: Squares that touch in the net are never opposite.
Don't count all 9 cubes on a face as having 1 painted face.

learn.hook: Some solids are so perfect that every face is the same regular shape. There are only five of them!
points: Arranging puzzle: use one clue at a time and keep checking the order.
An icosahedron has 20 faces, all equilateral triangles. 5 faces meet at each corner.
A dodecahedron has 12 faces, all regular pentagons. 3 faces meet at each corner.
Count edges smartly: icosahedron 20 faces × 3 sides ÷ 2 = 30 edges; dodecahedron 12 × 5 ÷ 2 = 30 edges (each edge is shared by 2 faces).

The five Platonic solids: tetrahedron (4 triangles), cube (6 squares), octahedron (8 triangles), dodecahedron (12 pentagons), icosahedron (20 triangles). Build them with straws (edges) and clay (corners).

example.q: How many straws and clay balls do you need to build a cube?
steps: A cube has 8 corners → 8 clay balls

learn.reallife: Some footballs are made of pentagons and hexagons, and some dice in board games are shaped like icosahedrons!

games.title: Line up the shapes
games.prompt: Use the clues: Circle is first. Square is just after Circle. Triangle is last. Star is between Square and Triangle.

quiz.q: Clues: The triangle is left of the circle. The square is right of the circle. The star is left of the triangle. What is the order from the left?
quiz.explain: Star is before triangle, triangle before circle, circle before square.
steps: Star is left of triangle; triangle is left of circle; square is right of circle.
quiz.mistake: Uses only some of the clues

quiz.q: What shape are the faces of an icosahedron?
quiz.explain: All 20 faces of an icosahedron are equilateral triangles.
steps: All of them are equilateral triangles.
So the faces are equilateral triangles.
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with the dodecahedron

quiz.q: What shape are the faces of a dodecahedron?
quiz.explain: A dodecahedron has 12 regular pentagon faces.
steps: All of them are regular pentagons.
So the faces are regular pentagons.
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with the icosahedron

quiz.q: An icosahedron has 20 triangle faces. Each edge is shared by 2 faces. How many edges?
quiz.explain: 20 × 3 = 60 sides, but each edge is counted twice: 60 ÷ 2 = 30.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that edges are shared

quiz.q: A dodecahedron has 12 pentagon faces. How many edges does it have?
quiz.explain: 12 × 5 = 60 sides, shared by 2 faces each: 60 ÷ 2 = 30.
quiz.mistake: Does not divide by 2

quiz.q: How many faces meet at each corner of an icosahedron?
quiz.explain: 5 equilateral triangles meet at every corner of an icosahedron.
steps: An icosahedron is made of equilateral triangles.
So 5 faces meet at each corner.
quiz.mistake: Uses 3 as in a cube

quiz.q: Which is NOT a Platonic solid?
quiz.explain: A cylinder has curved surfaces, not identical regular polygon faces.
steps: Platonic solids: tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, icosahedron.
Each has identical flat regular faces.
A cylinder has curved surfaces, so it is NOT a Platonic solid.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any solid counts

quiz.q: How many straws are needed to build a tetrahedron (4 triangle faces)?
quiz.explain: A tetrahedron has 6 edges, so 6 straws: 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Counts faces instead of edges

teach.ask: Gappu wants to build a cube with straws and clay. How many of each does he need, and why?
teach.praise: 12 straws for the edges and 8 clay balls for the corners!
teach.nudge: How many edges and corners does a cube have?

revise.summary: Solve arranging puzzles one clue at a time. The five Platonic solids have identical regular faces; count edges as faces × sides ÷ 2 since each edge is shared.
focus: Solve order puzzles from clues
Know the faces of the Platonic solids
Count edges and corners for straw models
remember: Icosahedron: 20 triangles, 5 meet at each corner, 30 edges
Dodecahedron: 12 pentagons, 3 meet at each corner, 30 edges
Cube: 12 edges (straws), 8 corners (clay balls)
traps: Don't forget to divide by 2 when counting edges.
Don't mix up icosahedron (triangles) and dodecahedron (pentagons).
